claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 was released, with the rewritten NCCL backend becoming the default for every nccl process group.
claims.excerpt: In PyTorch 2.15, every job that uses nccl runs on our rewritten backend by default.

claims.claim_text: The 2.15 release is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.
claims.excerpt: This release is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 adds one-sided transports for torch.distributed with NIXL as the first backend, marked API Unstable.
claims.excerpt: torch.distributed gains a Python transport API for one-sided data movement, with NIXL as the first backend.

claims.claim_text: On Apple Silicon, PyTorch's new grouped_mm gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput on an M3 Ultra, according to the PyTorch team.
claims.excerpt: the new MPS grouped_mm has a gemv path that gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput on an M3 Ultra.

claims.claim_text: The default PyTorch wheel moves to CUDA 13.2, with CUDA 13.4 GA wheels shipping alongside it for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and Windows.
claims.excerpt: The default PyTorch wheel moves to CUDA 13.2 (13.2.2 toolkit), with CUDA 13.4 GA wheels shipping alongside it for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and Windows.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or newer, and Python 3.10 is no longer supported.
claims.excerpt: Python 3.10 is no longer supported. PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or newer

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 requires macOS 15 or newer for MPS acceleration, dropping macOS 14 support.
claims.excerpt: PyTorch 2.15 requires macOS 15 or newer for MPS (Apple Silicon GPU) acceleration.

claims.claim_text: The rewritten NCCL backend's rollback path is setting TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or using the nccl-legacy backend.
claims.excerpt: nccl now selects the rewritten NCCL backend. Set TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 or use the nccl-legacy backend to restore the legacy ProcessGroupNCCL.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch's blog says a QR decomposition of a 512 x 512 matrix falls from about 7 seconds to 1.5 ms after solver rewrites.
claims.excerpt: QR of a 512 x 512 matrix falls from about 7 seconds to 1.5 ms, and triangular solves are now blocked.

claims.claim_text: The 2.15 release's Q&A webinar is scheduled for Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 11 AM PT.
claims.excerpt: Bring any questions you may have about PyTorch 2.15 to our Q&A webinar on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 11 AM PT.
